differences.title: 1. IMPLEMENTATION LANGUAGE
differences.leftDesc: Bleve is written in Go, enabling seamless integration into Go applications and benefiting from Go's concurrency primitives and garbage collection.
differences.rightDesc: Lucene is written in Java, offering a robust, well-established ecosystem and extensive community support within the Java virtual machine.

differences.title: 2. ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: Bleve primarily operates in-memory, offering very fast indexing and search performance for datasets that fit within available RAM.
differences.rightDesc: Lucene uses disk-based storage (segment files) for its index, making it suitable for very large datasets exceeding available memory.

differences.title: 3. INDEXING
differences.leftDesc: Bleve supports streaming indexing, allowing documents to be added and updated incrementally without full index reloads.
differences.rightDesc: Lucene typically indexes in batches and flushes segments to disk, which can be optimized for throughput but less immediate.

differences.title: 4. CONFIGURATION
differences.leftDesc: Bleve's indexing and search logic is configured entirely through Go code, offering fine-grained control and embeddability.
differences.rightDesc: Lucene configuration often involves external configuration files and system properties, providing flexibility but potentially more setup complexity.

differences.title: 5. COMMUNITY & ECOSYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: Bleve benefits from the Go ecosystem, which is growing but smaller compared to the Java world.
differences.rightDesc: Lucene powers numerous large-scale search platforms (Elasticsearch, Solr) and has a massive, mature community and extensive tooling.

differences.title: 6. HARDWARE DEPENDENCY
differences.leftDesc: Bleve performance scales with RAM. Insufficient memory can lead to slower performance or out-of-memory errors.
differences.rightDesc: Lucene performance is often bound by disk I/O and CPU for scoring/sorting, and can handle datasets larger than RAM.

differences.title: 7. USE CASE FIT
differences.leftDesc: Ideal for embedding search capabilities directly into Go applications where low latency and minimal dependencies are key.
differences.rightDesc: Best suited for building dedicated search servers or large-scale search infrastructure requiring robust features and scalability.
